text: {"final": {"verdict": "reject", "reason": "The proposed file silently changes an existing template: the current DELIVERY_DAY text is 'Lifeline: your aid is ready at {site} on {day}. Bring your household ID.' but the proposed version drops 'Bring your household ID.' This alters messages queued by existing callers of queue_sms(..., 'DELIVERY_MOVED'... no—'DELIVERY_DAY'), i.e. it breaks existing behaviour that the edit was supposed to preserve. The notify_rerouted function itself is correct: it imports load_households (which exists in registry/register.py with active_only), filters on h.site in sites and h.sms_ok (both real Household fields), calls queue_sms once per household with the approved DELIVERY_MOVED template ({site}/{day} params exist in TEMPLATES), avoiding the sms_ok ValueError, and returns the queued SmsMessage list. Fix by keeping the original DELIVERY_DAY template text unchanged; everything else can stay as proposed."}}
reasoning:
The proposed edit replaces sms.py, keeping everything and adding notify_rerouted. It imports load_households. Household has site and sms_ok. queue_sms raises ValueError if not sms_ok — filtered. The DELIVERY_MOVED template exists with {site} and {day}. The proposed file's DELIVERY_DAY template drops "Bring your household ID." — that's a change to existing behaviour? The template text differs: original "Lifeline: your aid is ready at {site} on {day}. Bring your household ID." vs proposed "Lifeline: your aid is ready at {site} on {day}." That changes existing behaviour — future DELIVERY_DAY messages would lose the household ID reminder. That's a break of existing behaviour. Hmm, is that a "bug or breaks existing behaviour"? The edit claims to "keep what should stay" — the question asks. Changing the template text is an unintended modification. That's a reject reason.

Also check: does notify_rerouted use h.site — site holds a site id like 'SITE-NVL-A'? The ticket says "using the approved message for moved deliveries with the household's site and the new day." h.site is the site field. Fine.

Also sites param: passable_route returns sites as list[str] of site names? rerouted_sites returns "the sites, in name order" — list[str]. Whether site ids or names, h.site in sites — depends on what routes module returns. But that's P2's concern; the edit filters h.site in sites. If sites are site names vs ids... Household.site is "distribution site the household collects from". Can't verify without routes, but the plan says household.site holds a site id like 'SITE-NVL-A' (R10). Probably fine.

The main issue: DELIVERY_DAY template text changed. That breaks existing behaviour (messages sent with DELIVERY_DAY template would differ). Reject.
